mantis_shrimp.title: THIS SHRIMP PUNCHES SO FAST IT BOILS WATER
mantis_shrimp.script: This is a mantis shrimp, and its punch is one of the most violent attacks in the ocean. Its front appendages snap forward with extreme acceleration, striking hard-shelled prey like crabs and snails. The blow is so fast that it creates vapor bubbles in the water. When those bubbles collapse, they release a second shock wave called cavitation, meaning the prey can be hit twice from a single strike. But the eyes may be even stranger. Mantis shrimp have an exceptionally complex visual system, with twelve color-sensitive channels in some species and the ability to detect polarized light. Each eye can move independently, constantly scanning the reef. So this small crustacean combines a weapon powerful enough to smash shells with a visual system unlike almost anything else on Earth.
mantis_shrimp.caption:
This tiny crustacean can strike so fast it creates a second shock wave underwater. 🦐💥
